mean: to take only a hurried, superficial look
lit: to look at flowers from a galloping horse

story.text: The Tang poet Meng Jiao failed the imperial examination several times and finally passed in middle age. In his joy he wrote the poem 'After Passing the Examination', with the lines: 'Proud in the spring breeze, my horse's hooves fly; in a single day I see all the flowers of Chang'an.' The rider who sees a whole city's flowers in a single day gave the idiom its image; it later came to mean a hasty look that takes in only the surface.

use.how: Adverbial or predicate, often with 地 or 式: 走马观花地看了看. Said of visits, reading or inspections that stay on the surface; often self-deprecating.

near.diff: 浮光掠影 describes a shallow impression or understanding; 走马观花 describes the hurried way of looking or visiting itself.

cue: You have one afternoon for an enormous museum and can only rush past the halls. How do you describe your visit?

ctx.s: 时间太紧，这次去北京只能{走马观花}地看看。
ctx.en: Time is too tight; on this trip to Beijing I can only have a quick look around.

ctx.s: 博物馆这么大，半天只能{走马观花}，下次再来细看吧。
ctx.en: The museum is so big that half a day only allows a quick walk-through; let's come back another time and look properly.

ctx.s: 很多旅行团一天跑五个景点，游客只能{走马观花}。
ctx.en: Many tour groups rush through five sights a day, so the tourists only get a fleeting look.

ctx.s: “那本书怎么样？”“我只是{走马观花}翻了一遍，说不上来。”
ctx.en: "What's that book like?" "I only flicked through it quickly, so I can't really say."

ctx.s: 领导下基层调研，不能{走马观花}，要坐下来听听老百姓的想法。
ctx.en: When leaders go down to do fieldwork, they mustn't just skim the surface; they need to sit down and hear what ordinary people think.

ctx.s: 他{走马观花}地看了一遍合同就签了字，结果吃了大亏。
ctx.en: He gave the contract a quick once-over, signed it, and ended up badly burned.

bad.s: 他学习非常认真，每篇课文都{走马观花}地读。
bad.en: (meant: he studies seriously and reads every text carefully)
bad.why: It means looking hastily and superficially, the opposite of careful reading.

bad.s: 他看问题很快，{走马观花}就能抓住重点。
bad.en: (meant: he is quick and grasps the key point at a glance)
bad.why: It criticises a superficial look; it is not praise for quick, sharp insight.

lit: everyone who has eyes has seen it together

use.how: Predicate, often in 是……的: 他的进步是有目共睹的. Said of achievements, efforts or changes that no one can deny, usually positive.

near.diff: 众所周知 opens a statement of a fact everyone knows; 有目共睹 says results or changes are visible to all, and is used as a predicate.
显而易见 is a conclusion that is obvious by reasoning; 有目共睹 is something everyone has actually witnessed.

cue: At the year-end meeting, the boss says nobody can deny how much the new hire has improved: everyone has watched it happen.

ctx.s: 这几年家乡的变化是{有目共睹}的。
ctx.en: The changes in my hometown over the past few years are there for all to see.

ctx.s: 她为这个项目付出的努力，大家{有目共睹}。
ctx.en: Everyone has seen how much effort she put into this project.

ctx.s: 经理在会上说：“小王的进步{有目共睹}，今年应该给他升职。”
ctx.en: The manager said at the meeting: "Xiao Wang's progress is plain for all to see; he should be promoted this year."

ctx.s: 这家医院近年来服务水平的提高{有目共睹}。
ctx.en: The improvement in this hospital's service in recent years is evident to everyone.

ctx.s: 公司的产品质量一直很稳定，这是{有目共睹}的事实。
ctx.en: The company's product quality has always been consistent; that is a fact everyone can see.

ctx.s: 他的成绩{有目共睹}，你凭什么说他是靠关系上来的？
ctx.en: His record speaks for itself; what makes you say he got there through connections?

bad.s: {有目共睹}，地球是圆的。
bad.en: (meant: as everyone knows, the earth is round)
bad.why: It cannot open a sentence as 'as everyone knows'; this idiom is a predicate about results everyone has seen.

bad.s: 这个秘密只有我们两个人{有目共睹}。
bad.en: (meant: only the two of us know this secret)
bad.why: It means seen by everyone; it cannot describe something only a few people know or saw.

lit: made clear to every family, known in every household

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 这个故事家喻户晓; 家喻户晓的人物. Said of stories, people, songs or brands known to ordinary people throughout a country or region.

near.diff: 举世闻名 is famous across the whole world; 家喻户晓 is familiar to ordinary families within one society.

cue: A character from an old folk tale is so familiar that every grandmother and every child in the country knows his name.

ctx.s: 孙悟空在中国{家喻户晓}，连小孩都知道他。
ctx.en: The Monkey King is a household name in China; even small children know him.

ctx.s: 这首歌一夜之间变得{家喻户晓}。
ctx.en: Overnight, this song became known in every home.

ctx.s: 这个牌子的酱油在我们那儿{家喻户晓}，几乎每家厨房都有一瓶。
ctx.en: This brand of soy sauce is a household name where I'm from; almost every kitchen has a bottle.

ctx.s: 那部电视剧播出以后，演主角的演员成了{家喻户晓}的明星。
ctx.en: After that TV series aired, the lead actor became a household name.

ctx.s: “你没听说过梁山伯与祝英台？这可是{家喻户晓}的故事啊！”
ctx.en: "You've never heard of the Butterfly Lovers? Everybody knows that story!"

ctx.s: 为了让防火知识{家喻户晓}，社区每个月都组织宣传活动。
ctx.en: To make fire-safety knowledge known in every home, the neighbourhood runs an awareness event every month.

bad.s: 这件事我们部门三个人都{家喻户晓}了。
bad.en: (meant: all three people in our department know about this)
bad.why: It describes something known across a whole society, and its subject is the thing known, not the people who know it.

bad.s: 他对历史{家喻户晓}，什么都知道。
bad.en: (meant: he knows everything about history)
bad.why: It says something is widely known, not that a person is knowledgeable. It cannot take the knower as its subject.

lit: the whole world has heard its name

use.how: Mostly attributive: 举世闻名的长城; also predicate. Said of places, works, people or products admired worldwide; typical of writing, guides and speeches.

near.diff: 家喻户晓 is known in every home of one society; 举世闻名 is famous across the whole world.
举世瞩目 is the world's attention on an event happening now; 举世闻名 is lasting fame.

cue: A tour guide introduces an ancient monument that visitors from every continent heard of long before they arrived.

ctx.s: 长城是{举世闻名}的古代建筑。
ctx.en: The Great Wall is a world-famous ancient structure.

ctx.s: 景德镇的瓷器{举世闻名}，很多外国游客专门来买。
ctx.en: Jingdezhen porcelain is famous worldwide, and many foreign tourists come specially to buy it.

ctx.s: 导游说：“我们现在看到的，就是{举世闻名}的兵马俑。”
ctx.en: The guide said: "What we're looking at now is the world-famous Terracotta Army."

ctx.s: 这位钢琴家不到三十岁就已经{举世闻名}了。
ctx.en: This pianist was already world-famous before turning thirty.

ctx.s: 谁能想到，这个{举世闻名}的品牌最初只是一家小作坊？
ctx.en: Who would have thought this world-famous brand started out as a small workshop?

ctx.s: 凭着这部小说，他从一个普通教师变成了{举世闻名}的作家。
ctx.en: With this novel he went from an ordinary teacher to a world-famous writer.

bad.s: 我们村的豆腐{举世闻名}，邻村的人都来买。
bad.en: (meant: our village's tofu is well known around here)
bad.why: Its scope is the whole world; it is wrong for fame that reaches only the next village.

bad.s: 这家公司因为造假{举世闻名}。
bad.en: (meant: the company became notorious for fraud)
bad.why: It is admiring fame; it is not used for notoriety earned by wrongdoing.

story.text: Yang Chufu, a minister of Jin, stopped at the town of Ning on his way home from a mission. The innkeeper, Ning Ying, admired him so much that he left home to follow him, but soon turned back. When his wife asked why, he said Yang was too harsh, and that he flowered but bore no fruit; such a man gathers resentment, and Ning Ying feared he would share in the harm before he gained anything.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 内容华而不实; 华而不实的人. Criticises people, writing, plans or objects that look impressive but have nothing solid behind them.

near.diff: 中看不中用 is colloquial and mostly about objects that look good but do not work; 华而不实 also judges people, words and plans.

cue: A consultant's proposal has beautiful slides and grand slogans, but not one concrete step anyone could take.

ctx.s: 这个网站做得花里胡哨，有用的信息却没几条，真是{华而不实}。
ctx.en: This website is all bells and whistles, but there's hardly any useful information on it: all show, no substance.

ctx.s: 他的报告写得很漂亮，但内容{华而不实}，没有一个具体办法。
ctx.en: His report is beautifully written, but it is all show with not one concrete measure.

ctx.s: 老师提醒我们：写作文要真诚，不要追求{华而不实}的辞藻。
ctx.en: The teacher reminded us: write sincerely and don't chase showy, empty phrases.

ctx.s: “这个装修方案太{华而不实}了，钱花了不少，住起来却不方便。”
ctx.en: "This renovation plan is all flash and no substance; it costs a lot, but the place would be inconvenient to live in."

ctx.s: 有些年轻人只注重包装自己，难免显得{华而不实}。
ctx.en: Some young people care only about packaging themselves, and inevitably come across as all style and no substance.

ctx.s: 选合作伙伴，我宁要踏踏实实做事的人，也不要{华而不实}的人。
ctx.en: When choosing a partner, I'd rather have someone who works steadily than someone who is all show.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜又好看又好吃，真是{华而不实}。
bad.en: (meant: the food looks good and tastes good too)
bad.why: It is a criticism meaning showy but empty; it cannot praise something attractive and substantial.

bad.s: 他穿着很朴素，看起来{华而不实}。
bad.en: (meant: he dresses plainly and looks unpretentious)
bad.why: The first character means showy; plain, modest dress is the opposite.

lit: to rise again from East Mountain

story.text: Xie An of the Eastern Jin dynasty lived for years in retirement at East Mountain in Kuaiji, turning down every offer of office and spending his time with friends and family. Around the age of forty he finally entered public service, rose to become chief minister, and guided Jin through the war with Former Qin that ended in victory at the Fei River. A return to power after retirement or defeat came to be called rising again from East Mountain.

use.how: Predicate: 他三年后东山再起. Said of a person, team or business that returns to success after failure, defeat or retirement.

near.diff: 卷土重来 is coming back after defeat to try again, and can describe unwelcome things returning; 东山再起 is regaining one's former standing.

cue: A businessman lost everything when his firm went bankrupt; five years later he runs a bigger company than before.

ctx.s: 他生意失败以后没有放弃，三年后又{东山再起}了。
ctx.en: After his business failed he didn't give up, and three years later he made a comeback.

ctx.s: 别灰心，你在这一行的名声还在，总有机会{东山再起}。
ctx.en: Don't lose heart; your reputation in this field is still intact, so there's always a chance to make a comeback.

ctx.s: 这家老字号曾经差点倒闭，没想到靠网上销售{东山再起}。
ctx.en: This old brand nearly went under, but surprisingly it bounced back through online sales.

ctx.s: 记者问：“您退休多年，这次复出是想{东山再起}吗？”
ctx.en: A reporter asked: "You've been retired for years; is this return an attempt at a comeback?"

ctx.s: 这位歌手沉寂了十年，新专辑一出就{东山再起}，又红遍了全国。
ctx.en: After ten quiet years, this singer made a comeback the moment the new album came out, and is famous across the country again.

ctx.s: 他心里清楚，失去了大家的信任，想{东山再起}就难了。
ctx.en: He knew that, having lost everyone's trust, a comeback would be hard.

bad.s: 感冒好了没几天，又{东山再起}了。
bad.en: (meant: a few days after recovering, the cold came back)
bad.why: It is a person or group regaining position, not an illness or problem coming back.

bad.s: 他第一次创业就{东山再起}，赚了很多钱。
bad.en: (meant: his very first business was a big success)
bad.why: A comeback needs an earlier fall or retirement; a first-time success is not a comeback.

use.how: Mostly attributive with 的: 前所未有的挑战; also predicate. Said of scale, change, feelings or situations never seen before, in the world or in one's own life.

near.diff: 史无前例 is weightier, 'unprecedented in history', for major events; 前所未有 also fits personal experience.

cue: On her first day in charge of the whole team, she feels a pressure unlike anything she has experienced in her life.

ctx.s: 这次考试的难度{前所未有}，很多同学都没做完。
ctx.en: This exam was harder than any before it; many students didn't finish.

ctx.s: 第一次站上这么大的舞台，她感到一种{前所未有}的紧张。
ctx.en: Standing on such a big stage for the first time, she felt a nervousness she had never felt before.

ctx.s: 人工智能给翻译行业带来了{前所未有}的挑战。
ctx.en: Artificial intelligence has brought unprecedented challenges to the translation industry.

ctx.s: “这么热的夏天，在我们这里真是{前所未有}。”
ctx.en: "A summer this hot is unheard of around here."

ctx.s: 搬到乡下以后，他享受到了{前所未有}的安静。
ctx.en: After moving to the countryside he enjoyed a quiet he had never known.

ctx.s: 退休后第一次一个人出国旅行，奶奶觉得{前所未有}地自由。
ctx.en: Travelling abroad alone for the first time after retiring, Grandma felt freer than she ever had.

bad.s: 我们每年春节都举行这个{前所未有}的活动。
bad.en: (meant: we hold this special event every Spring Festival)
bad.why: An event held every year has happened before, so it cannot be unprecedented.

bad.s: 这种情况以前{前所未有}过。
bad.en: (meant: this has never happened before)
bad.why: It already contains 'before' and 'never'; adding 'before' and the experience marker guo again is redundant and ungrammatical.

mean: to waste all the effort already made

story.text: The Qin general Bai Qi had won victory after victory and was about to march past the Zhou domain to attack Liang. The adviser Su Li urged the Zhou ruler to warn him with a story: the archer Yang Youji could hit a willow leaf at a hundred paces, but an onlooker said that if he kept shooting until his arm tired and missed once, all his earlier success would be thrown away. So too Bai Qi: one failed campaign, and his past achievements would count for nothing.

use.how: Predicate, often as a result or warning: 一下午的工作前功尽弃; 现在放弃就前功尽弃了. Said when a slip or setback makes all earlier work count for nothing.

near.diff: 功亏一篑 is failing right at the last step; 前功尽弃 stresses that all the earlier work is wasted, at whatever stage.
半途而废 is choosing to quit halfway; 前功尽弃 is the result, earlier effort wasted, often by a mistake.

cue: Your computer crashes before you save, and an entire afternoon's writing is gone.

ctx.s: 电脑突然死机，文件没保存，一下午的工作{前功尽弃}。
ctx.en: The computer suddenly froze before I saved the file, and a whole afternoon's work was lost.

ctx.s: 减肥最怕半夜吃东西，一顿就可能让你{前功尽弃}。
ctx.en: The danger in dieting is late-night eating; one meal can undo all your efforts.

ctx.s: 妈妈提醒他：“戒烟最难的是头几个月，你现在抽一根，就{前功尽弃}了。”
ctx.en: His mother reminded him: "The first few months of quitting are the hardest; smoke one now and it'll all be for nothing."

ctx.s: 培养了几个月的细菌被污染了，整个实验{前功尽弃}，只能从头再来。
ctx.en: The bacteria cultured for months got contaminated; the whole experiment was wasted and had to start over.

ctx.s: 拼图拼了一个星期，弟弟一碰桌子，全散了，真是{前功尽弃}。
ctx.en: I spent a week on the jigsaw, then my little brother knocked the table and it all fell apart: a week's work for nothing.

ctx.s: 病刚好一点就停药，很容易{前功尽弃}，医生让他一定吃完。
ctx.en: Stopping medicine as soon as you feel a bit better can easily undo the treatment, so the doctor told him to finish it.

bad.s: 他学了三年钢琴，弹得越来越好，真是{前功尽弃}。
bad.en: (meant: three years of piano have paid off)
bad.why: It means earlier effort was wasted; it cannot describe effort that has paid off.

bad.s: 这个项目刚开始，还什么都没做，就{前功尽弃}了。
bad.en: (meant: the project failed right at the start)
bad.why: It needs earlier work to be lost; nothing done means nothing to waste.

mean: worries back home or behind one that hold one back
lit: the worry that makes one look back over one's shoulder

use.how: Noun, usually object of 没有, 解决, 免除: 解决员工的后顾之忧. Said of concerns about family, home or livelihood left behind while one goes off to work, study or fight.

cue: A woman takes a job in another city; her parents promise to look after her child so that she need not worry about home.

ctx.s: 有父母帮忙带孩子，她出国读书就没有{后顾之忧}了。
ctx.en: With her parents helping with the child, she could study abroad without worrying about home.

ctx.s: 学校为参加集训的运动员安排了补课，解决了他们学业上的{后顾之忧}。
ctx.en: The school arranged extra lessons for athletes away at training camp, so they need not worry about falling behind in their studies.

ctx.s: “家里有我，你放心去比赛，不要有{后顾之忧}。”
ctx.en: "I'll take care of things at home; go and compete with your mind at ease."

ctx.s: 孩子没人管，我怎么能在外地安心工作？这就是我最大的{后顾之忧}。
ctx.en: With no one to look after my child, how can I work away from home in peace? That's my biggest worry.

ctx.s: 有了养老保险，他辞职创业时少了一份{后顾之忧}。
ctx.en: With a pension in place, he had one less worry holding him back when he quit to start a business.

ctx.s: 村里办起了托管班，外出打工的父母终于免除了{后顾之忧}。
ctx.en: Once the village set up an after-school care class, parents working in the cities were finally freed from worry about their children.

bad.s: 明天要考试了，我有很多{后顾之忧}，怕考不好。
bad.en: (meant: I'm anxious about tomorrow's exam)
bad.why: It is a worry about what is left behind (home, family, livelihood), not anxiety about what lies ahead.

bad.s: 他是个{后顾之忧}的人，总是想太多。
bad.en: (meant: he is a worrier who overthinks)
bad.why: It is a noun for a specific worry, not an adjective for a personality. It cannot describe what kind of person someone is.

mean: the whole story, the ins and outs
lit: where the dragon comes from and where the vein runs to

story.text: The phrase comes from traditional Chinese geomancy (fengshui). Geomancers likened a mountain range to a dragon and its unbroken ridge to a vein, and when judging a site they spoke of where the dragon came from and where the vein ran on to. The phrase was later extended to the origin and course of any matter.

use.how: Noun, usually 事情的来龙去脉, object of 讲清, 弄清, 了解. Said of the background and full course of an event, problem or idea.

near.diff: 前因后果 stresses cause and effect; 来龙去脉 is the whole course of a matter from its start to where it stands now.

cue: Before judging a quarrel between two colleagues, the manager wants to hear exactly how it started and how it developed.

ctx.s: 你先别生气，听我把事情的{来龙去脉}讲清楚。
ctx.en: Don't get angry yet; let me explain the whole story first.

ctx.s: 警察花了一个星期，才把这笔钱的{来龙去脉}查清楚。
ctx.en: It took the police a week to trace where this money came from and where it went.

ctx.s: “这个词是怎么来的？”“它的{来龙去脉}可复杂了，我慢慢跟你说。”
ctx.en: "Where does this word come from?" "Its history is quite complicated; I'll take you through it."

ctx.s: 新来的同事不了解项目的{来龙去脉}，开会时常常插不上话。
ctx.en: The new colleague doesn't know the project's background, so in meetings he often can't join in.

ctx.s: 这本书详细介绍了丝绸之路的{来龙去脉}。
ctx.en: This book gives a detailed account of the Silk Road from its origins onward.

ctx.s: 只看了一个新闻标题就下结论，你连{来龙去脉}都没搞清楚。
ctx.en: You drew a conclusion from one headline; you don't even know the ins and outs.

bad.s: 他说话很有{来龙去脉}，大家都爱听。
bad.en: (meant: he speaks in a well-organised way)
bad.why: It is a noun for the background and course of a matter, not a quality of speech; it cannot describe how well someone talks.

bad.s: 我昨天把作业的{来龙去脉}都做完了。
bad.en: (meant: I finished every part of my homework yesterday)
bad.why: It means how a matter began and developed, not all the parts of a task.
